rationale: A wins because it keeps the angles inside the four walls of the supplied facts. "Wise's stablecoin rollout will be decided by regulators, market by market" is a clean policy angle built from the actual region-by-region approval fact; B's "The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes" invents the numbers a reporter would demand first. B has sharper proof questions, but it also promoted hypothetical material as kept work, which is how decent strategy dies in the inbox.
gaps_in_A: "stablecoin settlement is crossing into regulated, mainstream B2B money movement" is a hair too big for one launch with an unnamed stablecoin, unnamed partner, and unnamed live markets. Keep the "test" frame until the missing names exist.

"which bank fees and float revenue get squeezed" needs one more gating proof item: whether Wise is replacing correspondent-bank relationships or merely supplementing them, and what share of the £30B volume is business/eligible.

"the stablecoin is regulated" is too thin for the policy angle. A compliance reporter will ask regulated by whom, under which regime, and what happens to balances if the issuer or regulator interrupts the instrument.
"Next step: journalist-fit-check" is slightly premature unless the live market list is also confirmed, not just the stablecoin and partner.
gaps_in_B: "The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes" invents both the delay and the clearance time. The update says faster and cheaper; it does not give a three-day baseline or minutes-level settlement.
"Without a named customer this angle does not exist — do not pitch it as a hypothetical." Correct diagnosis, wrong behavior: B kept the angle anyway. That is self-aware padding.

"putting stablecoins on its balance-sheet flows" asserts custody or treasury exposure the update does not provide. Customers can hold and settle; that is not the same as Wise carrying stablecoin balances on its own balance sheet.
"the first time this flow is being described as a shipped feature" is an unsupported first-time claim. Launch does not equal verified novelty in the market or in Wise's prior disclosures.
